newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees Hong Kong fund at $32.5 billion by 1997.
newsitem.headline: China sees Hong Kong fund at $32.5 billion by 1997.

text.p: China's top policy maker for Hong Kong has said the British colony's land fund would reach HK$270 billion ($32.5 billion) by the transfer of power in 1997, Chinese media reported on Wednesday.

Lu Ping, director of the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office of the State Council, or cabinet, said the total would reflect an additional HK$100 billion ($12.8 billion) turned over to the territory at the handover, the China News Service said.

The additional funds represent money held in trust from sales of government land in Hong Kong. Half of the proceeds from Hong Kong government land sales go to the colonial administration and half are held in trust for the post-1997 authorities.
The joint Sino-British Land Commission determines how much land is sold each year in the territory before the transfer of power.
Speaking to Chinese officials of the Sino-British Land Commission, Lu said the additional funds would contribute to future stability of the territory's currency, the Hong Kong dollar.
The territory will be able to keep its separate currency, now pegged at 7.8 to one U.S. dollar, after 1997.
Hong Kong reverts to mainland rule at midnight on June 30, 1997, becoming a Special Administrative Region of China.
